speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing episodes of dizziness and vertigo; to help me identify the cause, could you describe exactly what those spinning sensations feel like and how long they last? Also, do you experience any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or nausea during these episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed description. Since the dizziness is position-dependent and you have a history of presbycusis, I need to clarify the exact nature of these positional changes: does turning your head in bed, looking up, or rolling over specifically trigger the spinning sensation? Additionally, have you noticed any new hearing loss, ear fullness, or tinnitus in the affected ear?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The clinical presentation of brief, position-dependent vertigo in a 70-year-old patient is classic for this condition. I recommend performing the Dix-Hallpike maneuver to confirm the diagnosis.
